title: The Moon Borrows Joel's Sneakers
skyStory: June kicks the door open and the last sliver of the waning moon is still loitering in Aries, Joel's own sign, like a houseguest who found the good snacks. It is only thirteen percent lit and it does not care. Mars lends it a pair of sneakers. The moon does one lap of the sky, panting, and declares itself an athlete.

reading: A first-of-the-month itch is crawling up your arms: new calendar, new page, new everything. The moon is visiting your sign on its way out the door, so the energy is borrowed and a little sweaty. Use it for exactly one fresh start. Not five. The [[Knight of Wands]] is tapping his watch.

Somewhere around 10:40 am you will open a notebook and find a list you wrote in March. Half of it is done and you never crossed it off. Cross it off now, with ceremony, one line at a time, while saying each item out loud. This is not bragging. This is accounting for joy you already earned and forgot to collect.
joel.mission: Write the word JUNE in big letters on something you will see all day, then add one tiny goal underneath it in small letters.
joel.omen: A runner in a red shirt passing you twice. The month is lapping you on purpose, cheering, not racing.
joel.stoneWhy: your own fire, home for a visit
joel.elementWhy: the moon is warming up in Aries

reading: The first day of June arrives smelling like cut grass and somebody else's barbecue. The Wood Rat sniffs the air, assesses the situation and decides the month is acceptable, pending review. You are allowed to hold the review for a week. Nobody gets to rush a Capricorn verdict.

Around lunch a person will ask you to explain how something works. Your hands will start before your mouth does. Let them. By the end, the listener will understand the thing and also feel slightly hypnotised, which is the Life Path 11 side effect nobody warns them about. Take the compliment that follows without deflecting it even once.
nancy.mission: Rename one boring file, folder or list today with a name so dramatic it makes you snort when you see it.
nancy.omen: Lilac on the breeze before noon. It means a small kindness is already on its way to you, stamped and addressed.
nancy.stoneWhy: steady ground for a fresh month

together.text: Send each other one goal for June, exactly seven words long, no more and no less. Count on your fingers if you must. Pin the other person's goal somewhere you will trip over it. On the thirtieth, report back in exactly seven words again.

game.intro: The moon borrowed Joel's sneakers and went for a jog. Pick fast, guess faster.
game.question: If you had to sprint somewhere right now, where would you most like to end up?
